title: Levothyroxine: new prescribing advice for patients who experience symptoms on switching between different levothyroxine products
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
journal: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, Drug Safety Update, 19 May 2021
funder: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
result: Nearly 260 million packs of levothyroxine were dispensed in the UK between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2020. Between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2019 the MHRA received 335 Yellow Card reports of product substitution issue, condition aggravated or drug ineffective with levothyroxine, 47 from a healthcare professional; symptoms were mostly consistent with hypo- or hyperthyroidism, including fatigue, palpitations, anxiety and depression. Twelve reported recurrence on a second trial of the product; 27 included thyroid function results, of which 9 suggested a hypothyroid, 4 a hyperthyroid and 14 a euthyroid state. Causes were judged generally unclear. Advice: consider testing thyroid function when a patient reports symptoms after a product change; if symptoms persist, consider consistently prescribing one product known to be well tolerated, and if symptoms or poor control persist, an oral solution.
